prompt:
MODE: epic
Manager agent for flow: an event-driven fleet manager that drives pipelines to merge-ready PRs on the user's behalf, plus the pipeline autonomy policies that remove most human-checkpoint stalls without it.

CONTEXT (researched 2026-08-23 in pipeline i-want-add-new-feature; full analysis persisted in ~/.flow/state/i-want-add-new-feature.json under the `.answer` key — read it first with `jq -r '.answer' ~/.flow/state/i-want-add-new-feature.json`): of 30 live pipelines, 14 were stalled at designed human checkpoints (4 plan-pending-review, 3 gated, 2 interview/clarification, 1 needs-human, 2 epic-approved never launched, 5 crashed unresumed). Two classes: POLICY pauses (plan review, interview, clarification, crash resume, epic frontier launch — stopped by rule, not missing information) and JUDGMENT pauses (gated validation, needs-human diagnosis, epic redirects, cross-pipeline conflicts).

DECIDED DESIGN (weigh, but these were researched against primary docs on Claude Code 2.1.241):
- Event-driven, NOT a periodic poll loop: SendMessage notify_when_idle (one-shot, 12h expiry, main-conversation-only), messages to idle sessions start a new turn, Monitor tailing ~/.flow/state/*.json phaseLog, ScheduleWakeup 20-30min fallback heartbeat. Never poll ListAgents.
- Built-in cross-session messaging, NOT tmux capture-pane/send-keys. Observation stack: flow ls/state.json -> ListAgents (liveness) -> gh (PR truth).
- One manager with a thin cross-pipeline roster (slug/phase/PR/epic, shared-file overlap) persisted in ~/.flow/state/manager.json; deep per-pipeline work (plan critique, needs-human diagnosis) via one-shot Task sub-agents reading disk artifacts. No persistent per-pipeline sub-agents.
- Trust boundary stays mechanical: a peer message cannot answer AskUserQuestion or permission prompts; flow-merge-guard token still required — manager can NEVER merge a gated PR, tick SUBJECTIVE items, or override gates. gated => escalate-only. /flow-epic-run stays a deterministic playbook; the manager plays the human role above it.
- Manager runs fable high/xhigh; tmux window under the tmux launcher (claude --bg under plain-shell); identity env-first (FLOW_KIND=manager), never pane options.
- Permission class: pipelines run in the prompting class; a bypass-permissions manager would have every message HELD. Manager runs same class; set crossSessionInbound accept in ~/.flow/launch-settings.json.

CANDIDATE SLICES (5 PR-sized features; f1/f2 independently valuable without the manager):
f1 pipeline autonomy policies — --auto-approve-plan gated on the cross-model plan review, interview/clarification auto-adopt-recommended-after-timeout, flow feature resume --all-crashed.
f2 session addressability + inbound — flow feature create passes --name <slug>, sessionName recorded in state.json, crossSessionInbound accept in launch settings, flow ls shows it.
f3 supervisor-side manager inputs — /flow-pipeline names the exact pause points where a manager-session message counts as sanctioned input (approve plan, answer interview/clarification, redirect, resume); AGENTS.md named exemption like the Task-tool ones; stop-guard and merge paths untouched.
f4 flow manager start|stop|status verb + /flow-manager skill — the event-driven loop above, roster checkpointing, one-shot reviewer/diagnoser sub-agents, PushNotification to the user only on judgment pauses.
f5 epic driving — manager takes the human role in the epic-run playbook: launches frontiers, redirects features when a sibling PR changes a contract, escalates gated.

CONSTRAINTS: independent of the modernize-flow-s-supervisor-architecture epic (manager talks only state.json + messages + gh, so it survives the f6 workflow port either way). Don't re-introduce a tick loop or judgment sub-agent inside flow-epic-run. Verify all harness claims against current docs before anchoring features on them — specifically verify (against https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging and related current docs, via WebFetch or the claude-code-guide agent) the SendMessage notify_when_idle semantics/expiry, that messages to idle sessions start a new turn, the crossSessionInbound launch-setting and its HELD behaviour across permission classes, the `--name` session flag, ListAgents liveness fields, and Monitor/ScheduleWakeup availability. Record every verified claim and every claim that did NOT verify in design.md (anchor no feature on an unverified claim; downgrade it to an Open Question instead).

features.title: Pipeline autonomy policies: --auto-approve-plan, interview timeout, resume --all-crashed
features.description:
Add opt-in pipeline autonomy policies that resolve flow's policy pauses by rule instead of a human reply, without touching the gate, merge guard, or stop guard. (a) `flow feature create --auto-approve-plan` (persisted in `~/.flow/state/<slug>.json`, default from `~/.flow/config.json` `pipeline.autoApprovePlan`): at `/flow-pipeline` step 3's feature-intent end condition, when the cross-model plan review ran (`flow-plan-review` envelope `ran:true` with no demoted reviewer), plan.md's `## Recommendation` verdict is `Proceed`, and `flow-plan-lint` passes, the supervisor records `flow-state-update --phase-outcome 'auto-approve: <gate summary>'` and advances to step 5 in the same turn (mirroring the existing `advance-to-step-5` no-checkpoint route, with post-hoc disclosure of pre-ticked candidate issues in the PR body); when any part fails — including `review.gemini` off or a `ran:false` skip — it pauses at `plan-pending-review` exactly as today and records `auto-approve: skipped (<reason>)` in `phaseLog.outcome`. (b) `flow feature create --interview-timeout <duration>` (config `interview.autoProceedAfter`, off by default): at `triage-pending-interview`, `plan-pending-interview`, `triage-pending-clarification`, and `approval-pending-clarification`, when the question carries a `Recommended:` line, the supervisor schedules a session-scoped one-shot task (`CronCreate`, which fires only while the session is idle; pick a minute that is not :00/:30 to dodge the documented early jitter) whose prompt is the existing `proceed` escape verb from `references/interview-playbook.md`; re-arm it on resume; a late auto-`proceed` arriving at any other phase is a logged no-op; a clarification with no `Recommended:` line escalates `NEEDS HUMAN: clarification-timeout` after the timeout instead of guessing; record `interview: auto-proceed` in `phaseLog.outcome`. (c) `flow feature resume --all-crashed [--yes]` in `bin/lib/feature.ts`: expand to every row `bin/lib/ls.ts` `buildRows` marks `needsResumeHint` whose phase is non-terminal and not `triaged-no-change`, then reuse the existing multi-name preview/confirm and the launch-concurrency semaphore; also stop `flow ls` from listing `triaged-no-change` rows under 'pipelines needing resume' — label them `(answered)` and suggest `flow done`. Note: the live pipeline `i-want-improve-flow-ls` also edits `bin/lib/ls.ts` — rebase across it. Tests next door for each policy (argv/config parsing, state round-trip, the gate matrix, the ls row filter); SKILL.md step 3/step 1 prose and `interview-playbook.md` updated; the exact `phaseLog.outcome` strings are a documented vocabulary the manager (f4) consumes.

Part of epic `manager-agent-flow-event-driven` (feature `f1-autonomy-policies`) — design at `.flow/epics/manager-agent-flow-event-driven/design.md`.
features.rationale: Hides D1 — the policy thresholds that turn a rule-shaped pause into a rule; independently valuable with no manager, and the phaseLog.outcome vocabulary is what the manager later reads.
acceptanceCriteria: WHEN a pipeline launched with --auto-approve-plan reaches step 3's feature end condition with flow-plan-review ran:true (no demoted reviewer), a Proceed verdict, and a clean flow-plan-lint THE SYSTEM SHALL advance to step 5 in the same turn and append a phaseLog entry whose outcome starts with 'auto-approve:'

WHEN any part of that gate fails (review off/skipped, non-Proceed verdict, lint failure) THE SYSTEM SHALL pause at plan-pending-review and record 'auto-approve: skipped (<reason>)' in phaseLog.outcome

WHEN --interview-timeout elapses at an interview/clarification pause whose question carries a Recommended: line THE SYSTEM SHALL adopt every recommended answer via the proceed verb and continue; WHEN no Recommended: line exists it SHALL escalate NEEDS HUMAN: clarification-timeout

WHEN flow feature resume --all-crashed runs THE SYSTEM SHALL resume only dead-session rows at non-terminal phases other than triaged-no-change, after one confirmation (skipped with --yes), and flow ls SHALL no longer list triaged-no-change rows as needing resume

WHEN the test suite runs THE SYSTEM SHALL prove flow-stop-guard, flow-merge-guard, and flow-gate-decide are unchanged by this feature (no diff under bin/flow-stop-guard.ts, bin/flow-merge-guard.ts, bin/flow-gate-decide.ts)

features.title: Name every flow session by slug and accept peer messages unattended
features.description:
Make every flow-launched Claude session addressable by name and able to receive cross-session messages unattended. In `bin/lib/feature.ts`, `claudeArgv` (shared by the tmux and plain launcher backends) passes `--name <slug>` on create and resume; `bin/lib/epic.ts`'s epic-create and epic-run launch argv do the same with their window slug; each writer records `sessionName` in `~/.flow/state/<slug>.json` as an optional-additive `PipelineState` field in `bin/lib/state.ts` (absent ≡ unnamed, no migration). `ensureLaunchSettings` writes `"crossSessionInbound": "accept"` alongside the existing `hooks.UserPromptSubmit` seed-hook entry in the flow-scoped `claude --settings` file (`FLOW_LAUNCH_SETTINGS_PATH`, `~/.flow/launch-settings.json`), idempotently and preserving sibling keys, so a pipeline delivers peer messages regardless of the sender's permission class (a stricter project/local `refuse` still wins by documented precedence — say so in the docs). Add a launch-time pre-flight in the same helper family that warns (never blocks) when `claude --version` is below 2.1.236 or when any of `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC`, `DISABLE_TELEMETRY`, `DO_NOT_TRACK`, `DISABLE_GROWTHBOOK` is set to a value that disables feature-flag fetching (cross-session messaging is off then). `flow ls` gains a SESSION column (the recorded `sessionName`, `—` for rows without one) and `flow ls --json` exposes the field; document the new state field and settings key in `docs/configuration.md` and `references/consumer-repo-contract.md`. Note: the live pipeline `i-want-improve-flow-ls` also edits `bin/lib/ls.ts` — rebase across it. Tests: argv assertions for both backends and both epic verbs, state round-trip, launch-settings idempotency (existing hooks key byte-preserved on re-run), pre-flight warning matrix, ls rendering.

Part of epic `manager-agent-flow-event-driven` (feature `f2-session-addressability`) — design at `.flow/epics/manager-agent-flow-event-driven/design.md`.
features.rationale: Hides D2 — the identity/inbound carrier — behind one launch-path change; the walking-skeleton root every manager-shaped feature hangs off.
acceptanceCriteria: WHEN flow feature create, flow feature resume, flow epic create, or flow epic run launches claude THE SYSTEM SHALL include `--name <slug>` in the argv and record sessionName in the slug's state.json
WHEN ensureLaunchSettings runs THE SYSTEM SHALL leave ~/.flow/launch-settings.json containing both the seed hook and crossSessionInbound: "accept", byte-identical on a second run
WHEN flow ls renders THE SYSTEM SHALL show a SESSION column with the recorded name or — and flow ls --json SHALL expose sessionName
WHEN claude is older than 2.1.236 or a messaging-disabling env var is set THE SYSTEM SHALL print a one-line warning at launch and still launch

features.title: The manager-input trust contract: phase-keyed pause points, helper, AGENTS.md exemption
features.description:
Define, in prose and a pure helper, exactly where a message from the flow manager session counts as sanctioned input to a supervisor and where it never does — touching no gate, merge, or stop path. Add `skills/pipeline/flow-pipeline/references/manager-inputs.md` keyed by state.json phase (never by step number, so the contract survives the modernize epic's workflow port): `plan-pending-review` → `approve` / `redirect: <text>` / `cancel` / `pull #N into the plan` / `drop candidate #N`; `triage-pending-interview` and `plan-pending-interview` → answers in the playbook's `1a 2c` form or `proceed`; `triage-pending-clarification` and `approval-pending-clarification` → an answer; `checkpoint-pending-clear` → `continue`; `epic-design-pending-review` (in `/flow-epic-create`) → `approve` / `redirect: <text>` / `cancel`; an idle `/flow-epic-run` session → `launch-next` / `reconcile` / `status`; plus an explicit never-list: `gated` (escalate-only, including bug-callout redirects), `needs-human` (a resume is the CLI act `flow feature resume`, not a message), every permission prompt, the step-9 `AskUserQuestion` gate-override form, and `flow-merge-guard --record-override`. A message counts only when all three hold: the harness `<cross-session-message from=…>` sender name equals the constant `flow-manager` (export it from a new `bin/lib/manager-name.ts`), the body starts with `MANAGER:` and carries the policy token, and `flow-manager-inputs --check --phase <phase> --verb <verb> --token <token>` exits 0 — a new bare-name helper (`bin/flow-manager-inputs.ts`) that reads `~/.flow/manager/policy.json` (schema owned here: `{version, delegated: {<phase>: [<verbs>]}, token, startedAt}` — `token` is a random per-start value the manager echoes in every message, so a `MANAGER:` string that merely appears in an issue body, log, or fixture never passes the check; written only by `flow manager start` in f4, absent otherwise, so an unmanaged install honours nothing) and prints a JSON verdict. Every honoured message is recorded via `flow-state-update --phase-outcome 'manager-input: <verb> from <sender ref>'`. Add one pointer sentence at each pause point in `/flow-pipeline` SKILL.md (step 4, the interview and clarification pauses, checkpoint-pending-clear), `/flow-epic-create` step 7, and `/flow-epic-run`'s 'When to use'; add an AGENTS.md `## Don'ts` bullet `**Manager-input exemption: …**` in the same family as the AskUserQuestion and auto-issue-create exemptions (it is NOT a Task-tool exemption — `bin/skill-md-lint.test.ts`'s exactly-nine count and the AGENTS.md ↔ SKILL.md symmetry test must still pass), documenting the same-OS-user threat model. Add a lint test asserting `bin/flow-stop-guard.ts`, `bin/flow-merge-guard.ts`, and SKILL.md step 10 contain no reference to manager input. Tests for the helper's verdict matrix and the policy-file absence case.

Part of epic `manager-agent-flow-event-driven` (feature `f3-manager-inputs`) — design at `.flow/epics/manager-agent-flow-event-driven/design.md`.
features.rationale: Hides D3 — which pause points accept which verbs from the manager and the marker that turns delegation on — behind a phase-keyed reference + a mechanical check, so the trust boundary is not prose alone.
acceptanceCriteria: WHEN flow-manager-inputs --check runs with no ~/.flow/manager/policy.json THE SYSTEM SHALL exit non-zero for every phase/verb pair
WHEN policy.json delegates a verb for a listed pause phase THE SYSTEM SHALL exit 0 for that pair and non-zero for gated, needs-human, and any unlisted phase regardless of the file
WHEN the message's token does not match policy.json's token THE SYSTEM SHALL exit non-zero regardless of phase and verb
WHEN the repo's lint suite runs THE SYSTEM SHALL still count exactly nine Task-tool exemptions and SHALL fail if flow-stop-guard.ts, flow-merge-guard.ts, or SKILL.md step 10 mention manager input
WHEN a reader opens references/manager-inputs.md THE SYSTEM SHALL present one table keyed by phase with the accepted verbs and the explicit never-list

features.title: flow manager start|stop|status + the /flow-manager event-driven loop
features.description:
Add the manager: a `flow manager start|stop|status` verb (`bin/lib/manager.ts`, `verbs.ts`, completion scripts, help) and the `/flow-manager` skill (`skills/pipeline/flow-manager/SKILL.md`). `start` writes `~/.flow/manager/policy.json` (the delegated pause points per f3's schema plus a fresh random `token` the manager echoes in every message — default: interview/clarification `proceed`, `checkpoint-pending-clear` `continue`, epic `launch-next`; `plan-pending-review` `approve` only when a critic verdict exists, so until f5 lands an un-self-approved plan review is pushed to the user; `--delegate <list>` overrides), writes `~/.flow/manager/state.json` (`pid`, `procStartedAt`, `sessionName`, `startedAt`, `heartbeatExpiresAt`; every manager file lives under `~/.flow/manager/` and nothing under `~/.flow/state/`, which `listStates()` reads as pipelines — `flow-stop-guard` already exits 0 for a slug with no state.json, so no new phase or kind enters the pipeline vocabulary, and `flow ls` prints one manager status line from that file rather than a row), refuses to start when cross-session messaging is unavailable (f2's pre-flight), then launches one session with env `FLOW_KIND=manager FLOW_SLUG=manager`, `--name flow-manager`, `--model fable --effort high` (config `models.manager`, `--effort` override), the flow-scoped `--settings` file, and the flow skills home — a tmux window under the tmux launcher, or `claude --bg` under plain shell if f4 planning verifies that `--bg` composes with `--add-dir`/`--plugin-dir`/`--settings` and auto-runs the seed, else a named 'the manager needs the tmux launcher' refusal. `stop` SIGTERMs via the `pid`/`procStartedAt` liveness signal (`bin/lib/liveness.ts`, same rule as `plainTerminate`), removes `policy.json`, and leaves pipelines untouched; `status` prints the roster. The skill runs an event-driven loop and never polls: on start (and on every resume, since monitors do not survive resume) it builds `~/.flow/manager/roster.json` (per slug: phase, PR, epic, sessionName, worktree, liveness verdict, last phaseLog outcome, changed files from `gh pr view --json files` when a PR exists) from `~/.flow/state/*.json` plus one `ListAgents`, subscribes `SendMessage notify_when_idle:true` with no message body to every live pipeline session, arms one persistent `Monitor` over a script that emits one line when any state.json phase changes or a new state file appears, and creates a recurring `CronCreate` heartbeat every 20–30 min (non-:00/:30 minute; re-created before its 7-day expiry, `heartbeatExpiresAt` in the roster). Each heartbeat also reconciles: re-arm a subscription for every live non-terminal pipeline lacking one, so a dropped or expired notice costs at most one heartbeat interval. On each idle notice, Monitor line, or heartbeat it re-reads that slug's state.json, classifies the pause with `flow-manager-inputs`, and does exactly one of: send the sanctioned `MANAGER: <verb>` message carrying the policy token (a policy pause f1 left unresolved, read from `phaseLog.outcome`); hand a judgment pause to the dispatch seam (f5 plugs the critic/diagnoser in here; until then it escalates); escalate with a single `PushNotification` carrying the pause TLDR (from the idle notice's one-line status or `phaseLog`), the PR URL, and a roster line for `gated`, `needs-human`, exhausted retries, and any `NEEDS HUMAN`; or run `flow feature resume <slug> --force` for a dead session at a non-terminal, non-`triaged-no-change` phase — then re-arms that slug's one-shot subscription. The roster records dispatch counts per slug and phase: at most one automated `MANAGER:` message per slug per phase transition, then escalate (no wake/message ping-pong). Overlap detection: when two in-flight pipelines' changed files intersect, the later one gets a `MANAGER:` note at its next sanctioned pause and the roster records the overlap. Hard invariants, lint-anchored: never `gh pr merge`, never tick a Test Steps item, never `flow-merge-guard --record-override`, never `send-keys`, never poll `ListAgents` in a loop, never answer a permission prompt. AGENTS.md documents `/flow-manager` as a separate sanctioned session (like `/flow-epic-create`) with zero AskUserQuestion forms and, for now, zero Task fan-outs (f5 adds two). Acceptance includes a live round-trip test on a real paused pipeline and a measured answer to whether an idle manager wakes on a Monitor line (recorded in the skill's references).

Part of epic `manager-agent-flow-event-driven` (feature `f4-manager-loop`) — design at `.flow/epics/manager-agent-flow-event-driven/design.md`.
features.rationale: Hides D4 — the wake substrate (notices/events/heartbeat) and the roster shape — behind one verb + one skill; the thin slice where the manager's value first lands.
acceptanceCriteria: WHEN flow manager start runs under the tmux launcher THE SYSTEM SHALL open one session named flow-manager with FLOW_KIND=manager, write ~/.flow/manager/policy.json and ~/.flow/manager/state.json with nothing added under ~/.flow/state/, and flow ls SHALL show one manager status line and no manager pipeline row

WHEN a subscribed pipeline reaches a delegated policy pause THE SYSTEM SHALL deliver one sanctioned MANAGER: message within one idle notice and re-arm the subscription exactly once (live round-trip test on a real paused pipeline)

WHEN a heartbeat fires THE SYSTEM SHALL re-arm an idle subscription for every live non-terminal pipeline lacking one, and SHALL send at most one automated MANAGER: message per slug per phase transition before escalating

WHEN a pipeline reaches gated or needs-human THE SYSTEM SHALL send exactly one PushNotification with the pause TLDR and SHALL make no call to gh pr merge or flow-merge-guard --record-override (lint + transcript assertion)
WHEN a pipeline's recorded process is dead at a non-terminal phase other than triaged-no-change THE SYSTEM SHALL run flow feature resume <slug> --force at most once per event
WHEN the manager's transcript is audited THE SYSTEM SHALL show no ListAgents call outside start/resume and no time-driven wake more frequent than the heartbeat
WHEN flow manager stop runs THE SYSTEM SHALL terminate the manager process via the liveness signal, remove policy.json, and leave every pipeline's state.json unchanged

features.title: One-shot plan-critic and needs-human diagnoser sub-agents for the manager
features.description:
Give the manager its judgment: two one-shot Task sub-agents it spawns from the f4 dispatch seam, each reading disk artifacts only. `agents/core/flow-manager-plan-critic.md` receives a slug and reads `<worktree>/.flow-tmp/plan.md`, `.flow-tmp/plan-review.md` (the cross-model review, when it ran), `.flow-tmp/scout.md`, and the slug's `phaseLog` (including f1's `auto-approve: skipped (<reason>)`), then writes a typed verdict `<worktree>/.flow-tmp/manager-critic.json` (`{verdict: approve|redirect|escalate, rationale, redirect?: string, blockers: []}`) that the manager maps onto f3 verbs: `approve` → `MANAGER: approve`, `redirect` → `MANAGER: redirect: <text>` (bounded to one redirect per pipeline, then escalate), `escalate` → a PushNotification with the rationale attached. `agents/core/flow-manager-diagnoser.md` receives a `needs-human` slug, reads its state, the `NEEDS HUMAN: <reason>` tag, `flow-epic-judge-context context` output when the pipeline belongs to an epic, the PR's failing check logs (tail-bounded via `gh run view --log-failed`), and `.flow-tmp/*` result JSONs, and writes `<worktree>/.flow-tmp/manager-diagnosis.json` (`{cause, fixable_by: user|pipeline|unknown, recommended_next_action, evidence: []}`) which the manager attaches to the escalation push and, when `fixable_by: pipeline` and the reason tag is one of a named allowlist (e.g. `ci-hang` with CI now green, `gh-unavailable` after gh returns), actions by `flow feature resume <slug> --force`; everything else stays a push. Both definitions follow the existing agent conventions (frontmatter `tools:` allowlist Bash/Read/Grep/Glob/Write, no `model:` pin, per-spawn `model:` from `models.manager-critic` / `models.manager-diagnoser`), are resolved via the plugin-qualified `flow-module-core:` name with the same file-exists-guard + `general-purpose` fallback the other agents use, and are the only two Task fan-outs `/flow-manager` may call — documented bidirectionally in AGENTS.md's `/flow-manager` bullet and `references/exemption-contracts.md`-style contract text (not a tenth `/flow-pipeline` exemption; the nine-count lint is unchanged). Include schema validators for both JSON shapes next to the existing `bin/lib/*-schema.ts` pattern, a critic verdict-matrix test over fixture plans, and a design-checkpoint mode: for `epic-design-pending-review` the critic writes a one-paragraph critique that the manager attaches to the push but never converts into `approve` (design approval stays human).

Part of epic `manager-agent-flow-event-driven` (feature `f5-manager-judgment`) — design at `.flow/epics/manager-agent-flow-event-driven/design.md`.
features.rationale: Hides D5 — the critique/diagnosis prompts and verdict thresholds — behind typed verdict JSON and the f3 verbs, so tuning judgment never touches the loop.
acceptanceCriteria: WHEN a pipeline pauses at plan-pending-review with auto-approve skipped THE SYSTEM SHALL spawn exactly one plan-critic sub-agent, validate its manager-critic.json, and send approve or one bounded redirect, or escalate — never a second redirect

WHEN a pipeline reaches needs-human THE SYSTEM SHALL spawn exactly one diagnoser, validate manager-diagnosis.json, attach it to the escalation push, and only run flow feature resume when the reason tag is on the named allowlist and fixable_by is pipeline
WHEN an epic reaches epic-design-pending-review THE SYSTEM SHALL attach a critique to the push and SHALL NOT send approve
WHEN the lint suite runs THE SYSTEM SHALL find exactly two named Task fan-outs for /flow-manager in AGENTS.md and still exactly nine /flow-pipeline Task-tool exemptions

features.title: The manager plays the human role above /flow-epic-run
features.description:
Let the manager drive epics without changing the `/flow-epic-run` playbook (no tick loop, no judgment sub-agent, no autonomous redirect inside it). Extend `/flow-manager` with the epic recipes and the roster's epic fields (`epic.slug`, feature id from state.json's `--epic` membership, sibling PRs and their changed files): (1) when a state row reaches `epic-approved` (the user's own approve at the design checkpoint), merge the design PR only if `/flow-epic-create` opened it, CI is green, it is mergeable, and its body has zero unchecked `- [ ]` items — the auto-merge rubric's own condition — else push an escalation; then run `flow epic run <slug>` (tmux-only by hard constraint; under the plain launcher push a 'needs the tmux launcher' escalation instead) and subscribe to the epic-run session by name; (2) at each epic-run idle, reconcile via `flow epic status <slug> --json` + `flow-epic-dag --frontier <manifest> --completed <ids> --launched <ids>` and send `MANAGER: launch-next` while the frontier is non-empty and in-flight features are below `epic.maxParallel` (`bin/lib/epic-config.ts`), one launch per notice; (3) when a sibling feature merges, intersect the merged PR's changed files with each in-flight sibling's worktree diff and plan, and at the affected sibling's next `plan-pending-review` send the already-sanctioned `MANAGER: pull #N into the plan`; for a sibling already past planning, push a note instead of redirecting; (4) `gated ⇒ escalate-only`: the push includes the `flow-epic-membership` line so the user sees the epic impact; (5) `epic-design-pending-review` is never answered by the manager (f5's critique rides the push). Record every epic action in the roster with the epic-run session `[ref]`. Tests: recipe matrix over fixture manifests/status boards, a frontier-vs-maxParallel launch test, the changed-files overlap test, and a lint asserting `skills/pipeline/flow-epic-run/SKILL.md` gained only f3's one pointer sentence.

Part of epic `manager-agent-flow-event-driven` (feature `f6-epic-driving`) — design at `.flow/epics/manager-agent-flow-event-driven/design.md`.
features.rationale: Hides D6 — the epic-driving recipe (merge the design PR, launch, redirect a sibling) — above an unchanged playbook, reusing already-sanctioned replies.
acceptanceCriteria: WHEN an epic reaches epic-approved with a green, zero-unchecked design PR under the tmux launcher THE SYSTEM SHALL merge it, run flow epic run <slug>, and subscribe to the epic-run session; WHEN any condition fails it SHALL push an escalation and merge nothing
WHEN the epic-run session goes idle with a non-empty frontier and in-flight features below epic.maxParallel THE SYSTEM SHALL send exactly one MANAGER: launch-next per idle notice
WHEN a sibling PR merges with changed files overlapping an in-flight sibling still at plan-pending-review THE SYSTEM SHALL send MANAGER: pull #N into the plan; otherwise it SHALL push a note only
WHEN a child feature is gated THE SYSTEM SHALL push one escalation including the flow-epic-membership line and SHALL never merge or override it
WHEN the lint suite runs THE SYSTEM SHALL prove skills/pipeline/flow-epic-run/SKILL.md contains no loop, polling, or Task language beyond its existing invariants
